title: Qualify the candidate and establish the 1.0 freeze
goal: Demonstrate a stable API/SPI/schema on one candidate commit in real consumers and make the release gate and post-1.0 compatibility comparison blocking.
context: Architecture phase D (revision 2, D4, D6, D9, D12), detailed 2026-10-14 with the owner answers M17 (D24–D27): 1.0 is the starting point, so the gate, baselines, bench reference, docs and CHANGELOG carry no 0.x scenario or history. Approximate size: M. The candidate closes the one pre-1.0 transition; only fixes demonstrated necessary by qualification are allowed (knowledge/p4-execution#conventions). Physical extraction remains conditional future work; tagging v1.0.0 is the owner's act after the plan (D27).

consumes: The relocated implementation and evidence from P1–P3
produces: 1.0 version metadata and a public history that starts at 1.0.0 (D24, D25)
One green qualification of conditions 1–9 on the supported matrix, locally and in GitHub Actions, with every demonstrated fix recorded
Compatibility comparator over the attribute manifests and format fixtures with an intentional-break drill (I18, D26)
Blocking compatibility CI with a guarded baseline pointer, and a release workflow that runs the whole qualification graph before split and release
Race, consistency and load evidence recorded as the 1.0 reference (I21, I22 as amended by D24)
Documentation of every frozen contract, the compatibility promise and the CHANGELOG [1.0.0] section
Frozen candidate, baseline pointer and gate evidence (gate.md)
boundaries: 1.0 requires every amended release condition on the candidate commit
A tag cannot bypass the candidate qualification matrix
A PR cannot replace the compatibility baseline silently
Future relocation keeps FQCNs, formats, migration basenames and data
No item creates or pushes a tag; pushes only to origin feat/1.0-candidate under the owner gate CI-PUSH

include: API generator, ApiManifestTest and tests/Arch rules in blocking mode
Driver/cache/replica, race, load and consumer suites

pitfalls: Regenerating a manifest on the same branch does not prove compatibility
continue-on-error checks do not qualify a distribution
Release validation on a tag must cover the qualified candidate
Interface additions, named parameters, defaults and closed-enum cases can break implementers
Tags v0.3.0 and v0.7.0 exist: stable-tag resolution must require major >= 1
A baseline pointer cannot name its own commit: the pointer commit follows the candidate and changes nothing else
Internal check FQCNs are JSON keys of doctor-checks.json but not identities: match by key
The owner's uncommitted test-refactor files (tests-nightly.yml, bin/test-db.php, phpstan.neon, parity tests) must not be swept into commits
CI was red on Laravel 11 at the last pushed commit; P3 never ran in CI

validation.procedure: Verify the ten release conditions as amended by D24 (knowledge/p4-execution#gate) on the candidate commit with the evidence in artifacts/evidence/P4/gate.md, and prove that the compatibility comparison and the tag-triggered release graph fail on intentional breaking fixtures (interface method, parameter rename, closed-enum case, payload key, migration basename) through the unit catalogue and bin/compat-drill.sh.
validation.expect: Every condition green with reproducible evidence on one candidate commit; every intentional break is rejected; the pointer commit changes only compatibility.json.

deliverables: Frozen API/SPI, schema and machine-format baselines (candidate pointer in compatibility.json)
1.0.0 release notes, frozen-contract docs and the AI-agent instruction in UPGRADING.md (D25)
1.0 reference load profile and race evidence

sections.title: Mandatory design inputs
sections.text:
The detailing session for P4 reads these before authoring any item (`show` of this phase is the entry point; the list is mandatory):

```bash
P='python3 <task>/scripts/plan.py'; ID=2026.10.10-№1-AZGUARD-CORE-STABILIZATION
$P get $ID knowledge/architecture --section release-gate
$P get $ID knowledge/architecture --section invariants
$P get $ID knowledge/architecture --section api-compatibility
$P get $ID knowledge/architecture --section transition-policy
$P get $ID knowledge/architecture --section risks
$P get $ID knowledge/contracts            # all sections
$P get $ID knowledge/identities            # all sections
$P get $ID knowledge/upgrade-map            # all sections (becomes UPGRADING.md)
$P get $ID knowledge/type-map            # rules
$P get $ID D4
$P get $ID D6
$P get $ID D9
$P get $ID D12
$P get $ID D13
$P get $ID D16
```

Rules for the detailed items:

- **D16 (owner M15): 0.7.0 is no compatibility constraint.** Before authoring items, re-evaluate every 0.7.0 installation, adoption, published-copy and populated-fixture scenario (D11, B18, knowledge/architecture#persistence, release-gate condition 5) and propose its removal or simplification as an explicit decision for the owner; implement the reference without shims; symbol changes go to the AI-agent migration instruction in docs/upgrade.md, not to a machine upgrade map.
- Each item lists in `reads` (with `section`, `required: true`) the reference sections it implements; a phase-bound document that no item reads is reported by `design-done` (`phase_documents_unread`) and must be resolved before the phase counts as detailed.
- Items cite their type-map rows by current FQCN in `scope.include`; an item may not move, rename or re-mark a type differently from `knowledge/type-map`.
- If `design-done` reports a pack over the 256 KB budget, move the binding of a reference document from the phase to the items that read it (`plan.py unlink … --kind applies_to`, `plan.py link …`) — never drop the read.
- Baselines are taken from the candidate; the intentional-break fixtures cover one example per frozen category of `knowledge/identities` and `knowledge/contracts`.

sections.title: Exit criterion
sections.text: The documented 1.0 release gate is satisfied on one candidate commit with linked evidence, and no architecture boundary, contract or format remains undecided.
